text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

Shareholders of brewer Brok approved a capital raise, public offering and bourse entry, with the firm's main shareholder, AHK Beteiligungsgesellscaft of Germany, proposing to buy shares from employees.

Polish secret services during Communism sent information about the Vatican to Moscow and East Berlin. Dresden Prelate Dieter Grande says it was possible that Vatican officials close to the Pope spied for the KGB.

In August Poland's business climate remained good, with 0.5 percent more firms recording growth in production and services, the Central Planning office said in its monthly poll. About 35 percent of firms increased exports.
The dollar value of Polish exports should increase by 10 percent though the country should show a trade deficit of about $10 million, a foreign trade institute said.

The final date for the privatisation of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) has been delayed to the end of March next year. Bidding are consortia led by Creditanstalt Financial Advisers, Citibank and Lehman Brothers, with the winning firm or consortium to receive 50 to 65 percent of the bank's shares.
Wednesday should see the signing of a long-term contract for the supply of gas from Russia to Poland. It could happen that Poland will have to accept more gas than it is capable of using.
The American journalist Carl Bernstein said the U.S. government gave the Solidarity movement $50 million from 1981 to 1989, though Americans involved in the donations say the sum was much lower.
